title: Analytical techniques
overview: Interpret chromatography, ¹H NMR and ¹³C NMR spectra, combining evidence from several techniques to identify structures. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Interpret chromatography and calculate Rf values.
Use ¹³C NMR to count carbon environments and identify chemical environments.
Use ¹H NMR chemical shift, integration, splitting and D₂O exchange.
Combine chromatographic, mass, infrared and NMR evidence to determine structures.

definitions.definition: Separation by different affinities for stationary and mobile phases.
Distance moved by a solute divided by distance moved by the solvent front.
NMR signal position δ in ppm relative to a reference.
Relative area of a ¹H NMR signal, proportional to the number of equivalent protons.
Signal multiplicity caused by coupling to neighbouring non-equivalent protons.
The electronic surroundings that make nuclei equivalent or non-equivalent.
The ion corresponding approximately to the intact molecule in a mass spectrum.

sections.title: Chromatography
content: A component travels further when it has greater affinity for the mobile phase and weaker attraction to the stationary phase. In TLC/paper chromatography, Rf is dimensionless and only comparable under identical conditions. One spot can suggest purity but co-elution is possible.
bullets: Measure from the baseline to the centre of each spot.

examples.label: Key relationship
examples.content: Rf: Rf=distance moved by solute/distance moved by solvent front

sections.title: ¹³C NMR
content: The number of signals gives the number of distinct carbon environments, reduced by symmetry. Chemical-shift ranges indicate environments such as alkyl, C–O/C–X, C=C/aromatic and C=O. Routine proton-decoupled ¹³C spectra do not use peak integration to count carbons.
bullets: Use the syllabus data table rather than memorised exact shifts.

sections.title: ¹H NMR
content: Count proton environments, use δ for functional surroundings, integration for relative proton numbers and the n+1 rule for n equivalent neighbouring protons on adjacent atoms. OH/NH signals may be broad/variable and disappear on D₂O exchange; they may not split predictably.
bullets: Simplify integration ratios to whole-number proton counts.
Apply splitting only between appropriate non-equivalent neighbouring protons.

sections.title: Combining evidence
content: Start with molecular formula or M⁺ and degree-of-unsaturation ideas, identify functional groups from IR/tests, then construct fragments from NMR integration/splitting and join them while matching every carbon/proton environment. Chromatography can distinguish mixture components and monitor purity.
bullets: A final structure must explain every signal and observation.
Predict the spectrum back from the proposed structure as a check.

formulas.label: Rf
formulas.expression: Rf=distance moved by solute/distance moved by solvent front

formulas.label: ¹H splitting
formulas.expression: n equivalent neighbouring H ⇒ n+1 lines
formulas.note: Use only where coupling assumptions are valid.

examTips: Create an evidence table: datum → structural implication → remaining possibilities.
Do not identify a whole molecule from one peak; combine every technique.
Use precise chemical vocabulary, balanced equations and stated conditions; link every observation or trend to particles, bonding or equilibrium.
commonMistakes: Counting ¹³C peak height as the number of carbons.
Applying n+1 splitting across oxygen or to exchangeable OH/NH without justification.
Accepting a structure that leaves an unexplained signal.

quickRecall.question: Why can Rf values only be compared under the same conditions?
quickRecall.answer: Solvent, stationary phase and temperature affect the partitioning and travel distance.

quickRecall.question: What does the number of ¹³C signals show?
quickRecall.answer: The number of distinct carbon environments, accounting for symmetry.

quickRecall.question: What information does ¹H integration give?
quickRecall.answer: The relative number of equivalent protons producing each signal.

quickRecall.question: What does a D₂O exchange peak reveal?
quickRecall.answer: An exchangeable O–H or N–H proton signal disappears.

quickRecall.question: How should a proposed structure be checked?
quickRecall.answer: Predict all expected NMR environments, integrations/splitting and ensure all other evidence is explained.
